AccessKey.description: An engine-issued key, as inspected. The token itself is never stored or returned again.
AccessKey.title: AccessKey

AllocationRead.description:
The answer to reading one actor's allocation (#168): the allocation's record, and its amounts as
the payment provider reports them now. ``allowance`` is what the allowance read answers for the
same actor, by the same read of the provider: what was allotted (``granted``), what is spent, what
is available, and the provider's status. An enterprise's engine reads an actor's allowance here.

``allowance`` is ``None`` when the provider could not be read: unknown, never zero. The record is
the engine's own and is answered either way.
AllocationRead.title: AllocationRead

Allowance.description: The allocation as the provider reports it. A cap that can overshoot: funds are not reserved.
Allowance.title: Allowance

EscrowAccount.description:
One on-chain escrow account of the clearinghouse's wallet, as the payment provider reports it
(#167): the TicketBroker deposit and reserve of one sender on one chain. Both are in ETH, exact to
the wei. They are what the provider's on-chain listener has confirmed through
``confirmed_through_block``, not the chain's head: the engine reads no chain itself.

``sender`` is the wallet's public address, which the provider already reports. No key material, no
keystore path and no RPC address is here.
EscrowAccount.title: EscrowAccount

KnownActor.description: One row of the operator's actor list (D46, D48): allotted, signed in, or both.
KnownActor.title: KnownActor

Money-Input.description: An exact amount in one currency. Serialized as a decimal string, never a float.
Money-Input.title: Money

Money-Output.description: An exact amount in one currency. Serialized as a decimal string, never a float.
Money-Output.title: Money

OnboardedTenant.description:
The answer to onboarding a tenant (D83, #165): the tenant, whose id is the id of the grant the
provider created for it, and its first tenant admin key. The key's token is in the answer to the
first successful call only: the engine keeps its hash, so a repeat of the reference answers
``token: null`` and ``replayed: true``, as issuing any access key does.
OnboardedTenant.title: OnboardedTenant

SecretRef.description:
A SecretStore handle, or an opaque receipt for a credential the work engine holds. Which one is the
actor's ``credential_custody``, never the text of ``ref``.
SecretRef.title: SecretRef

SetAsideUsage.description:
A provider usage row the cost sync could not read or store, left out of every cost (#114, C13).

Kept so reconciliation can name what is missing. ``raw`` is the row as received, for the log only: the
store never holds it.
SetAsideUsage.title: SetAsideUsage

SignerReadiness.description:
Whether the signer answered its identity call just now (#167): the unauthenticated call every
payment begins with. ``ready`` says the signer is reachable where the engine calls it and signed
with the wallet's key. It does not say the wallet is funded, that the signer's price feed or event
stream is up, or that it can reach the payment provider: those are the signer's own ``/readyz``, on
a listener the engine is not given.
SignerReadiness.title: SignerReadiness

TenantGrant.description:
A tenant with its grant, as the payment provider reports it (D83). The tenant's id is the grant's
id. ``unallocated`` is what is left to allot; the provider, not the engine, refuses an allocation
larger than it. ``spent`` is the tenant's payment usage: what its allocations have spent, the revoked
ones included (#166). ``allocated_unspent`` is what its allocations still hold (#167): for each one,
what it was allotted less what it has spent, and nothing for one that has spent more, so an overdrawn
allocation takes nothing off another's. A revoked allocation holds nothing: what it had not spent is
back in ``unallocated``. The two together are what the tenant may still spend.
TenantGrant.title: TenantGrant

TenantState.description: The answer to pausing or resuming a tenant: the status its grant now has.
TenantState.title: TenantState

TopUpRequest.description: A top-up of an allocation or of a tenant's grant. The path names which: the body names no grant.
TopUpRequest.title: TopUpRequest

UnspentGrants.description:
What the tenants whose grants are in one currency may still spend (#167): for every grant the
provider holds in that currency, whatever its status, the grant's total less what its allocations
have spent, and never less than zero for one grant. ``grants`` is how many grants were summed.
Nothing is converted: a deployment with grants in two currencies has two of these.
UnspentGrants.title: UnspentGrants

UsageRow.description: One Batteries ``GET /v1/usage`` item. Batteries remains the authority; this is a cached copy.
UsageRow.title: UsageRow

WalletReport.description:
What a clearinghouse admin watches the wallet by (D82, #167): the deposit and reserve, the total
of unspent grants, and the signer's readiness. Each amount is in its own currency. Nothing is
converted between ETH and a grant's currency, and no margin is computed: the report states, and a
person judges.
WalletReport.title: WalletReport

get.description:
The clearinghouse's runner list, in livepeer/node's discovery format: what an enterprise's
engine reads as its ``LPB_DISCOVERY_URL``. The document is served as the clearinghouse read
it. Any credential of a tenant may read it.

200.description: The livepeer/node `/discovery` document the clearinghouse last read.

503.description: The clearinghouse has read no runner list yet.

schema.title: Response List Tenants V1 Clearinghouse Tenants Get

post.description: Create the tenant's grant and its first tenant admin key, whose token is shown once.

get.description: The tenant's allotted actors and the people an identity provider signed in (D46, D48).

schema.title: Response List Actors V1 Clearinghouse Tenants  Tenant Id  Actors Get

get.description:
The actor's allocation: its record, and as `allowance` what the payment provider reports for
it now (allotted, spent, available, status). `allowance` is `null` when the provider could not
be read.
The grant's total, its unallocated balance and its status.

schema.title: Response List Tenant Keys V1 Clearinghouse Tenants  Tenant Id  Keys Get

post.description: Issue an auditor key for the tenant, or, as a clearinghouse admin, another tenant admin key.
Pause or resume the tenant by pausing or resuming its grant.

get.description:
One page of the tenant's payment records, oldest first: the payment provider's usage rows
for the tenant's grant, and none of another tenant's. ``cursor`` is the last page's
``next_cursor``, which is empty on the last page.

The wallet's deposit and reserve as the payment provider has confirmed them, the total of
unspent grants for each currency, and whether the signer answers. Nothing is converted
between currencies and no margin is computed.

tags.description: Served by an engine in its `both` or its `clearinghouse` role (`LPB_ROLE`): these routes are 404 on an engine in its `work` role, which uses a payment clearinghouse and is not one.
tags.name: clearinghouse half

tags.description: Served on the private listener only, when the deployment has one (`LPB_HTTP_PRIVATE_PORT`): these routes are 404 on the public listener. A deployment with one listener serves them there. An engine in its `clearinghouse` role always has a private listener.
tags.name: private listener
